Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ac4fcfdaf67ece3b38fa2102d9aaf7f4eba1b498`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23306 (body; triage `6151767880`; claim `6158175677`; os-dev-report `6160278988`), PR #23386 (body, 15-file list, net diff against `main` at the head, +1053 −66), the check-runs on the head (read once, about 2026-10-14T03:39Z, not polled), and the committed source at the head and at `origin/main` by `git show` / `git grep` only.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public-surface changes the diff implies — each named.**

- `@objectstack/spec/contracts` gains exactly four exports: `IFileAttachmentService` (interface), `AttachFileInput` (interface), `AttachedFile` (interface), `FILE_ATTACHMENT_SERVICE` (const, `'file-attachments'`). RIGHT: the `contracts` shards of `api-surface/` and `export-origins/` carry exactly those four rows and nothing else; 0 removed, 0 renamed. Interface plus slot constant only, no runtime logic in spec (Prime Directive #2). `data: Buffer` matches `IStorageService.upload`'s existing `Buffer` in the same file. A sibling slot rather than a member of `IStorageService` is RIGHT: that contract is the adapters' blob store, and an adapter holds no data engine to write rows through.
- `@objectstack/service-storage` registers one more kernel service, `file-attachments`, declared in `providesServices` and registered in `init()` on every path with every dependency read per call (`getEngine` / `getStorage` / `getLimitsSnapshot`), armed at `kernel:bootstrapped`. RIGHT: both `ObjectKernel` (`kernel.ts`, phase 3.5) and `LiteKernel` (`lite-kernel.ts`) fire `kernel:bootstrapped` after every `kernel:ready` handler, and `gatedEngine` is assigned only inside the branch where this plugin installed its own `sys_attachment` hooks, so a kernel with no hook-capable engine keeps the verb at `503`. `buildKey` and the three new `storage-limits.ts` exports are package-internal: `index.ts` re-exports neither (`storage-limits` contributes types only), so the package's published widening is the one service.

**The verb's refusals and their envelopes — each named.**

- `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (standard code): field-by-field, before any read or write; `organizationId` is required and nullable, so "no organization" is stated. RIGHT.
- `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (standard): before `kernel:bootstrapped` or with no engine, before any write. RIGHT, and the right direction (refuse rather than write a row no gate judged).
- `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (ADR-0112 ledger, `@objectstack/service-storage` owner key): the shared `uploadSizeRefusal` verdict, before a byte or a row. RIGHT.
- `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` (standard): parent missing, or walled into another organization than `organizationId`; one sentence for both, so the answer says nothing about the other organization. RIGHT. Named, not a defect: the upload door answers the same cross-organization parent `403 ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` because its verdict is an EDIT-access verdict that folds existence in; the verb has no caller to ask, so its verdict is existence under the wall. Two verdict kinds, two envelopes, both documented on the contract docblock.
- `403 FILES_DISABLED`: not the verb's own — `plugin-audit`'s `enforceFilesCapability` on the `sys_attachment` `beforeInsert`, which carries NO `isSystem` early return (`audit-writers.ts` lines 2241-2260), so it judges the system insert exactly as a user's. RIGHT: the gate's decision, never a copy of it.
- Any other hook refusal propagates unchanged; the one store-wrapped case (engine refusal of the `sys_file` write surfacing as `StorageMetadataStoreError`) is declared in the PR's acceptance notes, see ③.

**The upload doors' size refusal: a pure move.** RIGHT. On `main`, `storage-routes.ts` held `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE_STATUS = 413`, `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE_CODE: RegisteredErrorCode = 'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE'`, `uploadTooLargeMessage` and the predicate `maxUploadBytes === undefined || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes at-or-under maxUploadBytes` inside `requireWithinUploadLimit`. At the head the two constants, the message function (same rounding, same sentence) and the predicate live in `storage-limits.ts` as `uploadSizeRefusal`; `requireWithinUploadLimit` now sends `sendError(res, UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE_STATUS, UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE_CODE, refusal)`. All six door call sites are unchanged in position and in their `measured` lambdas (head 898 / 1030 / 1173 / 1187 / 1536 / 1546 against main 925 / 1057 / 1200 / 1214 / 1563 / 1573). Same status, same code, same words at every door; the claim's ⛔ on the catch-all 5xx arms and on `metadata-store.ts` is respected (neither touched).

**"No refusal leaves a committed `sys_file`" — traced on every path the code takes.** HOLDS.
- Before step ③ (validation, 503, 413, parent 404): nothing written.
- Step ③ `createFile` writes the row `pending`; a throw there leaves nothing.
- Step ④ upload failure: `discard` deletes the bytes then the pending row; on a byte-delete failure the row is kept `pending` on purpose, and `sys_file` declares `retention: { maxAge: '7d', onlyWhen: { status: 'pending' } }` with the reap guard deleting a pending row's bytes (`system-file.object.ts` line 202, `attachment-lifecycle.ts`), so the residue is reclaimed and never `committed`.
- Step ⑤: the `sys_attachment` insert and the `status: 'committed'` update run inside `engine.transaction(cb, base)`. The store's `updateFile` builds its own `{ isSystem, tenantId }` context without the handle, and that is still inside the unit: ObjectQL's `transaction` runs the callback under `runOpenedUnit`'s `AsyncLocalStorage` store, so operations issued during the callback bind to the transaction's connection ambiently (`engine.ts` 19992-20044, contract docblock "operations issued during the callback ALSO bind to it ambiently"). An insert refused by a gate never reaches the commit. A commit refused after the insert rolls back under an owned transaction; under a joined one or on an engine with no `beginTransaction` (both reported `owned: false` — verified in `engine.ts`, the degrade is "honest", `{ owned: false }`), the verb deletes the attachment row it inserted (`EngineDeleteOptions` extends `BaseEngineOptions`, so `{ where, context }` in one object is the contract's shape). Either way `discard` then removes bytes and pending row.
- A rollback of an OUTER transaction the verb joined (after the verb returned) unwinds the commit update and the attachment row together, leaving a pending row for retention.
- Crash mid-call: pending row plus bytes at most, reclaimed by retention. Declared by the dev as the one UNPINNED half (ablation A2b, committed-first stayed green); the card's invariant itself is pinned by A2 (4 red) and A4/A5 (3 red).

**Security read — does the verb, acting as the system, open any write the upload door would refuse for the same parent and organization?** NO, within everything that is a property of the parent, the organization and the bytes. The door's `sys_attachment` insert is judged by three kinds of gate: (a) size, `enable.files`, and the parent's existence under the tenant wall — the verb runs all three, two through the identical code and the third (the wall) through the package's one wall-column resolver (`createWallOrganizationResolver`, the `computeTenantField` mirror, never a hard-coded column) over a system read by id; (b) the caller-identity gates — EDIT on the parent through `mayEditParent` / sharing `checkEdit`, the `sys_attachment` create grant, `uploaded_by` stamping, the refused-attach tombstone of the caller's own upload (#22466) — all of which return at `if (ctx?.session?.isSystem) return;` (`attachment-access-hooks.ts` line 519) or are the security layer's user checks; a system producer has no identity for them to judge, which is the context the card prescribes, and `uploaded_by` is `required: false` on `sys_attachment` so the null stamp is a legal row whose uploader shortcut nobody can later claim; (c) the organization stamp: the verb writes `sys_file` through `StorageMetadataStore.createFile` with a `StorageWriteContext` (the `tenantId` → `injectTenantOnInsert` channel the doors use) and `sys_attachment` with `{ isSystem, tenantId }`, in the parent's own organization or, for a global parent, the caller's — the same organization the door's session would stamp. Named, by design and documented: `organizationId: null` lets a system caller reach a parent in ANY organization and writes both rows into that organization. That is not a bypass of a door gate (no door exists for a session with no organization on a walled deployment) but it is a reach no door has; the consumer (#23307) must pass the mailbox's organization, never `null`, to stay walled. One more named point: the parent-wall refusal is the one check the verb OWNS rather than shares (the door's equivalent is the engine wall under a user session, which a system read cannot use); it is built on the shared resolver, pinned with its negative control (A3), and is the minimal addition the card's "parent outside the organization" acceptance requires — not a second copy of a door check.

**Composition parity.** When `plugin-audit` is not composed, neither the door nor the verb has an `enable.files` gate — same engine, same hooks, same answer; the verb is armed only after every plugin's `kernel:ready` handler, so no earlier write slips past a gate that is installed later.

### ② Semver level

RIGHT. `.changeset/23306-storage-attach-verb.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': minor` and `'@objectstack/service-storage': minor`, which is what the diff publishes: four additive exports on `@objectstack/spec/contracts` (0 removed, 0 renamed, no retired key, no tombstone owed) and one new registered service on `@objectstack/service-storage` (the route module's size refusal is a move with no change in any door's answer, and no new export reaches `index.ts`). `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` on the changeset body and `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body match the claim's `Clause-②: yes`; `readClause2Line` reads the arm as `widening` (the exact regex admits `(widening` followed by `:`, excluding only a word character or a pipe), so the declaration is `declared / yes / widening`, non-breaking, and `yes` takes at least `minor` — satisfied. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed (non-breaking). `Check Changeset` on the head: success. Pre-mode: spec at `18.0.0-next.0`, `minor` admitted (`check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 in the dev's gate list, and `Lint & Repo Gates` success on the head).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6160278988`: `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer or escalate there. Each `deviations` entry and each `out_of_scope_findings` entry, judged:

1. Files outside the claim's declared surface — `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`: forced by `check:tenant-audit-census` (the verb's two `sys_attachment` writes, both carrying a context, move the census 226 → 228; the diff shows exactly those two new ledger rows plus the mechanically re-derived figures and stamp). `packages/services/service-storage/package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`: a test-only `@objectstack/plugin-audit` devDependency so the `FILES_DISABLED` pin runs the real gate rather than a stand-in; the alias follows the package's existing `core` / `driver-sql` source-alias precedent, the lockfile change is the three-line importer entry only, `check:workspace-manifest-cycles` and `Validate Package Dependencies` are green. The claim said "stop on a breach and explain it in the report"; the dev explained each. ANSWERED: inside the card's scope, each forced and minimal.
2. Lockfile kept to the importer entry (an unrelated esbuild re-resolution dropped). ANSWERED, correct hygiene.
3. A temporary probe test committed then deleted on the branch; absent from the net diff (15 files, none named `zz-probe`). ANSWERED.
4. The `storage-routes.ts` extraction is a move; `main` (with PR #23346) merged before the PR opened; census conflict resolved by re-deriving. ANSWERED, verified in ① against `origin/main`.
5. "The card's parent-access hooks do not run under the system context the card prescribes." ANSWERED, not escalated: the hooks ARE in the verb's path (installed on the engine the verb writes through, and the verb is armed only after they are), and their system-context early return is their own pre-existing, declared design — the card itself prescribes the system context, and its Acceptance names three refusals (quota, files disabled, parent outside the organization), all of which run and are pinned with negative controls. What a system producer cannot be asked (a user's EDIT right) the card never listed as an acceptance refusal. The consequence belongs to the consumer: the producer, not the verb, decides which parent a file is attached to, with no per-user authorization — appropriate for inbound mail, and #23307's design should say so.
6. Harness attribution reminder versus AGENTS.md's model-free trailer pair: AGENTS.md followed. ANSWERED, correct in-repo.
7. The full `@objectstack/spec` local suite not measured locally (narrowed to `src/contracts`, declared). ANSWERED by the head's check-runs, recorded below as found.

Out-of-scope findings (noted, not filed): (a) a system call with `organizationId: null` against a global parent on a walled deployment surfaces the engine's `SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError` as a `StorageMetadataStoreError` rather than a 4xx — declared in the PR's acceptance notes, the doors' behaviour too by source reading, unmeasured; a composition error of the caller, acceptable as a note under Prime Directive #10. (b) On an engine with NO transaction, a process death between the attachment insert and the commit leaves an attachment row pointing at a pending row the reap guard reclaims after 7d — inferred, not reproduced; a note is the right carrier. (c) No docs page names the service; the contract docblock is its documentation and #23307's dev is the carrier. Accepted.

Scope against the card and triage `6151767880`: one verb in `@objectstack/service-storage`, declared as a service contract in `packages/spec/src/contracts/storage-service.ts` with its generated projections, one changeset, `service-mailbox` untouched, the catch-all 5xx arms and `metadata-store.ts` untouched. Direction "one writer, no second copy" held: size verdict shared by move, `sys_file` writer shared, `sys_attachment` judged by the engine's own gates, organization stamp through the shared channel; the one verb-owned check is named in ①. No governed surface in the file list (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/**` all absent); 1,119 changed lines, under the 3,000 ceiling; head repo equals base repo.

Check-runs on the head as found (read once, about 03:39Z): `Lint & Repo Gates` success · `Build Core` success · `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success · `Check Changeset` success · `Check PR Size` success · `Validate Package Dependencies` success · `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, the three `Lint · scoped` lanes, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (summary), `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, the three claim/path guards and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` all success · `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` in_progress, no `Test Core` summary yet · `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check · workspace` in_progress, no `TypeScript Type Check` summary yet · `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the sharded `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke` skipped (full-battery or opt-in, not PR-lane). The dev's own reading at the final head: 956 service-storage tests and 453 spec `src/contracts` tests green, both typechecks exit 0, `check:generated` 14 of 14 current. The landing seat reads the two pending summaries green before arming; `in_progress` is not a pass.
